clue.text: Prickly types beginning to cavil before start of play

indicators.note: the beginning of the word cavil is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening of a play is Act One, written ACT I

explanation.surface: Someone prickly begins by quibbling before a show has even got going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prickly types' looks like grumpy people, but means spiny plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Desert succulents covered in spines are the plainest example of prickly plants.

clue.text: Girl's given account in court — it's something special

indicators.note: in places pieces inside another

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl giving evidence in court proves exceptional.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something of outstanding quality is described informally as exceptional.

clue.text: It's Mother who cleans? An attractive quality

parts.note: a char is a cleaning lady
it's is short for it is, giving the word is
ma is mother

explanation.surface: Mum is the household cleaner: a charming trait.
explanation.walkthrough: A char, or charwoman, is an old British term for a cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal magnetism that draws people in is a compelling, attractive quality.

clue.text: Petty criminal in one clan's quiet

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are corrupted and rearranged

explanation.surface: A minor crook keeps silent inside a family clan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Petty criminal' reads as one phrase, but Petty is the definition and criminal the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trivial and of little importance is unimportant, or petty.

clue.text: Ready to abandon game

parts.note: ready money, or the readies, is cash; a quid is a pound
to ditch something is to abandon it

explanation.surface: Someone prepared to give up a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' as an adjective is the trap: here it is slang for cash, giving QUID, British slang for a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: The flying broomstick sport from the Harry Potter books is a fictional ball game.

clue.text: Having no Ecstasy, supply crack

indicators.note: having no means a letter is removed

parts.note: to equip is to supply
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A dealer without ecstasy supplies crack cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: The drugs picture misleads: 'crack' means a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A witty remark or wisecrack is a crack.

clue.text: One gaining ground learnt not to be impatient

indicators.note: gaining means one piece adds others after it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: ground, as in ground down, suggests the letters are crushed and reformed

explanation.surface: Someone making progress learned not to be impatient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a noun after 'gaining', but it is the past tense of grind, signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unwilling to put up with others is short-tempered, unaccepting, or impatient.

clue.text: Expression of disapproval of children acting like teenagers?

definitions.meaning: a cry rejecting the young, like down with tyranny
being in tune with youth culture, used of trendy adults

explanation.surface: A slogan against children, or adults behaving like adolescents.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase rejects children; idiomatically it praises adults who keep up with youth fashions.

clue.text: Capital put up after Turkey's quake

indicators.note: after places the next part behind the first one

parts.note: TR is the international code for Turkey

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: An earthquake strikes Turkey, and a capital city is built afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A small earthquake or shaking movement is a quake.

clue.text: Cardinal swaps sides, creating loathing

indicators.note: swaps sides says the two halves of the word change places

parts.note: a red hat is worn by a cardinal and stands for one

explanation.surface: A churchman defecting to the other side causes bitterness.
explanation.walkthrough: A cardinal's red hat stands for the cardinal himself; swap RED and HAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense dislike or detestation is a synonym of loathing.

clue.text: Saint oddly embraces chief supporter of lawlessness

indicators.note: embraces means one part holds another inside it
oddly signals that the letters of Saint are set out in a strange order

parts.note: arch as a prefix means chief, as in archbishop

explanation.surface: A holy figure strangely hugging a leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' tempts the solver to take alternate letters of Saint, but that gives only three; here it signals a reshuffle instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rejects all government and rule of law advocates lawlessness.

clue.text: Direction to conceal the ending of Oliver Twist

indicators.note: to conceal says one piece is hidden within another

parts.note: west is a compass direction

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: An instruction to hide how the Dickens novel Oliver Twist ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oliver Twist' reads as one title, but the clue splits it: Twist is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist something forcefully is to wrench or pull it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Tight-fitting blue clothes in Norway

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: to clothe something is to wrap around it

parts.note: sky blue, so blue can mean sky
N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: Close-fitting blue garments on sale in Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' looks like a noun, but it is a verb meaning covers.
explanation.definitionFit: Skinny jeans are slim, close-cut trousers, so the word describes snug clothing.

clue.text: Dawdler has to stick on second base

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: base means low, as in a low or base motive
to poke is to stick or jab

explanation.surface: A slow baseball player told to hold at second base.
explanation.walkthrough: The baseball picture misleads: 'base' is the adjective meaning low.
explanation.definitionFit: A slowcoach who lags behind others is an American informal word for a dawdler.

clue.text: Declare a cut in day care finally

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: SAT is short for Saturday
to sever is to cut

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Announcing a reduction in childcare provision, at last.
explanation.walkthrough: SEVER goes inside SATE, after its S, giving SSEVERATE after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To state something solemnly and emphatically is a formal way to declare it.

clue.text: Firm friend possessing millions treated nurse as equal

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: possessing means one part holds the others inside it

parts.note: a mate is a friend

indicators.note: treated suggests the letters of nurse are worked on and reshaped

explanation.surface: A company associate, very rich, treated a nurse as an equal.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are proportionate or of matching size are corresponding, or equal.

clue.text: Universal laughter after relative makes a fuss

indicators.note: after places these pieces behind the first one

parts.note: bro is short for brother, a relative
U is the film classification for universal
ha ha is the sound of laughter

explanation.surface: Everyone laughs when a family member kicks up a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy commotion or uproar over something trivial is a fuss.

clue.text: Beggar is baron, short of a few pounds?

parts.note: something short of a few pounds is lighter in weight

explanation.surface: A beggar is really a baron who has fallen on hard times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pounds' suggests money, but means weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Beggar is a mild British insult for a rascal or wretch, a synonym of this informal word.

clue.text: Miraculous conversion of errant Saul, heavenward bound?

indicators.note: bound means held in, so one piece is placed inside the others
conversion of signals the letters of errant Saul are changed into a new order

parts.note: heavenward means upward, giving up

explanation.surface: Saul's miraculous conversion on the road to Damascus, a straying soul bound for heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conversion' evokes Saul becoming Paul, but signals an anagram of ERRANT SAUL; 'bound' places UP inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Events beyond the laws of nature, attributed to divine power, are miraculous.

clue.text: Watery grave I rejected

indicators.note: rejected says that letter is thrown out

parts.note: grave means serious

explanation.surface: A watery grave, which I turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watery grave' is a stock phrase, but Watery is the definition and grave the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical term for fluid resembling or producing serum, a thin watery liquid.

clue.text: Raved about book enthusiastically, say

indicators.note: about suggests the letters of raved are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone gushed about a book with real enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the definition as an example: enthusiastically is one such word.
explanation.definitionFit: Enthusiastically is a word modifying a verb, an example of this part of speech.

clue.text: Close by mountains, moving river is risk

parts.note: a close is an end

indicators.note: moving says one letter shifts to a different position in the word

parts.note: a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: Being close to mountains with a shifting river is a hazard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' takes the R from the front of RANGE to the back, making ANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something in danger is to risk it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Spoke about what is displayed afresh in the Tate?

indicators.note: about means one part goes round another

parts.note: a rung of a ladder or chair is a spoke
eh is a way of saying what? when you have not heard

explanation.surface: Someone talked about what is on show at the Tate gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoke' looks like a verb but is a noun, a ladder's crosspiece. The Tate is a group of British art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintings hung again on a gallery wall have been displayed once more.

clue.text: In contact with contributor to group online

indicators.note: contributor to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone touching base with a person who posts to an internet group.
explanation.definitionFit: The preposition means resting on or touching, as in a hand laid on a shoulder.

clue.text: Having to remain in back, I look daggers

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
back says the word that follows is read in reverse

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look!
to be is to remain or exist

explanation.surface: Forced to stay at the back, I glare angrily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look daggers' is the idiom for glaring, but daggers is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The printer's dagger sign, also used to mark doubtful passages, has this Latin plural name.

clue.text: One after job of parish priest in Port of Spain, mostly

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Alicante is a port in Spain

explanation.surface: Someone seeking a parish priest post in Trinidad's capital, Port of Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port of Spain' is the Trinidad capital in the surface, but here it is a Spanish port, Alicante.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate who has put in a request for a position is seeking employment.

clue.text: Junior officer in navy, on vessel working late

indicators.note: in places one piece within another
in an across clue, one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: a sub is a submarine, a vessel
RN is the abbreviation for Royal Navy

indicators.note: working suggests the letters of late are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A junior naval officer on board ship, working late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in navy' looks like part of the definition, but the rank is an army one; navy gives RN.
explanation.definitionFit: A British army officer below the rank of captain is a junior commissioned officer.

clue.text: Adult stops commotion for part of the flight

indicators.note: stops means plugs, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a stir is a commotion
A is the film classification for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up calms a disturbance on part of an air journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests a plane, but means a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A single step is one unit of a staircase, which is called a flight.
